iterations.theme: Infrastructural collapse of Poljud and tactical analysis of the derby: Hajduk's pressing against Dinamo's weaknesses

sections.subtitle: Water polo conditions at Poljud: When umbrellas become mandatory equipment under the roof
sections.screenshot_description: Host Renato Špehar shows a photograph of soaked match reports from the press box at Poljud.
sections.content:
After a long international break, domestic football returned to the center of attention in the most dramatic way possible – with the biggest Croatian derby between Hajduk and Dinamo at Poljud. In a special edition of the podcast **Ofenziva**, host **Renato Špehar** welcomed analysts **Duje Granić**, **Luka Vujić**, and **Marino Durdov** to dissect the match in which the Blues took the lead with a goal by **Beljo** in the first half, only for the Split team to expressly equalize via an own goal just three minutes later, and then at the beginning of the second half reach a turnaround and a 2:1 victory through **Bamba**. Nevertheless, the football segment in the last half hour of the match fell into the background due to a biblical flood that turned the pitch into a swimming pool, and the game into complete anti-football.

**Duje Granić**, who watched the match live at the stadium with his colleague **Marko Štrkalj**, described the bizarre experience of staying in the Poljud press box, which was under a roof only in theory. While on one hand the atmosphere due to the home team's turnaround was fantastic and entertaining, on the other hand infrastructural chaos reigned.

- Journalists could not work on laptops because the rain was falling directly on the equipment despite the covered stadium.
- Media workers, including commentary positions, had to flee from their positions and hold umbrellas in order to perform basic work tasks.
- **Granić** vividly compared the last twenty minutes of the match to the historic Christmas match between the English and the Germans in the trenches of the First World War.

Although **Granić** admits that any pitch can become soaked due to extreme precipitation, he warns that such infrastructural failures at Poljud are unacceptable even for the standards of 2010, let alone today.

sections.subtitle: Cosmetic make-up or demolition: Why does Split urgently need a completely new stadium?
sections.screenshot_description: Luka Vujić explains the dilapidated state of the Poljud stadium structure.
sections.content:
The extreme downpour, the strongest since the July Ultra festival, arrived at a moment when the topic of stadium infrastructure in Croatia is at the peak of relevance. After the presentation of the new Maksimir project and the announcements by Prime Minister **Andrej Plenković** about the reconstruction of the Split stadium, a debate opened on whether such a derby sends a charming *vintage* picture or represents a disgrace for the league. **Luka Vujić** believes that the storm laid bare all the problems at the ideal moment and points out that a cosmetic renovation of Poljud simply makes no sense.

According to **Vujić's** words, the Split club desperately needs a completely new stadium, while maintaining two large stadiums in the city would be commercially unprofitable, which is best shown by the example of the poor management of the **Spaladium Arena**. Describing the actual condition of Poljud, **Vujić** presented a series of worrying details:

- The stairs leading to the press box and the stands are literally collapsing, and are supported by ordinary pieces of plank.
- During March, at the match against Osijek, the entire structure underfoot in the box was shaking to the extent that it seemed as if it would collapse at any moment.
- Two years ago, one of the load-bearing pillars of the stadium was tied with ordinary copper wire.

Apart from the pitch itself and the dressing rooms, absolutely everything needs to be replaced at Poljud. **Vujić** rejects arguments about preserving Poljud as a cultural good, reminding that this status was granted about ten years ago exclusively in order to draw money from European Union funds, which was ultimately not even done. Drawing a parallel with England, where the iconic **Highbury** and the old **Wembley** were demolished without hesitation, he concludes that stadiums are consumable goods and that Poljud is dearest to those who do not come to it at all. A temporary relocation of Hajduk and the renovation of **Park mladeži** would be expensive, but necessary steps. **Marino Durdov** added to this that the derby itself, despite the idle periods and hoofing of the ball after the 60th minute, was more interesting in content than many derbies in the last five or six years that were played in ideal conditions, but looked like a mud pit due to poor styles of play.

sections.subtitle: Tactical anatomy of the turnaround: Aggressive pressing that threw Dinamo into panic
sections.screenshot_description: Duje Granić with the help of a graphic display on the screen analyzes the mechanisms of Hajduk's high pressing.
sections.content:
Moving on to the tactical analysis of the first sixty minutes, before the water polo pitch made any meaningful combination play impossible, **Marino Durdov** highlighted Hajduk's extremely aggressive, almost 'mad' high pressing at the beginning of the second half as the key moment of the match. With that pressure on the back line, along with a congested midfield, the Split team threw Dinamo into complete panic and made it impossible for them to get out of their own half. Unlike Dinamo, who fell after scoring a goal, Hajduk showed mental toughness and the ability to continuously rise through the match despite their own mistakes.

However, **Durdov** warned of the chronic problem of communication and off-the-ball play in both teams, which was best seen in Dinamo's first goal. Before the goal itself, during a throw-in for the Blues, as many as three Hajduk players watched the thrower while an opposing player ran behind their backs and received the ball. A chain reaction of poor marking switches and a lack of vocal communication in defense followed, which led to **Beljo's** goal.

**Duje Granić**, with graphic displays, explained in detail the mechanisms of Hajduk's pressing which have become standard this season. When **Šego** and the wing forwards go out high onto the opposing center-backs, the full-backs must obligatorily follow that pressure and close the corridors. Unlike some previous matches where a winger like **Bamba** would rush forward without the support of the full-back and leave a gap, in this derby the synchronization and mutual support in the upper part of the pitch were at a top level. Dinamo practically the entire match, except for a couple of minutes between the two goals and the final chaos, did not have a period of dominance and control.

Looking back at the work of coach **Garcia**, **Granić** concluded that this match in a purely tactical sense was not drastically different from some previous derbies that Hajduk lost (such as the 2:0 defeat when **Hoxha** and **Bakar** scored). The key difference was in what **Garcia** himself emphasized at the press conference: **it is better to play 'badly' as a real team, than to play 'well' without team spirit**. Hajduk did not fall apart at any moment, and the top-notch approach was mostly manifested in the defensive phase.

sections.subtitle: New profiles in the midfield: How Del Moral brought the balance that Hajduk lacked for years
sections.screenshot_description: Luka Vujić talks about the importance of player profiles in Hajduk's midfield and the role of Del Moral.
sections.content:
One of the key deciding factors in the derby was the structure of Hajduk's midfield. Host **Renato Špehar** reminded of previous clashes at Poljud in which Hajduk also entered the pressing well, but would be easily outplayed due to the lack of physical power of the defensive midfielders. This time the Split team went out onto the pitch with clear profiles – a true 'six' and a true 'eight', whereby **Del Moral** excellently controlled the defensive spaces, while his partner in the middle brought technical power and calmness on the ball.

**Luka Vujić** agreed that there were almost no tactical surprises in the preparation of the match, rather the match was decided precisely by the profiles of the players on the pitch. Analyzing Hajduk's new midfield, **Vujić** highlighted several key elements:

- The technically more skilled midfielder in the pair proved to be one of the best reinforcements of this season because he processes the ball extremely quickly, receives it on the turn, and immediately passes it on without slowing down the game, along with a large amount of running.
- **Del Moral** was, right alongside **Bamba** and **Hrgović**, the best individual of the match. Although he is not technically dominant in the final third, his running, aggressiveness, and defensive reading of the game were invaluable.
- A comparison with previous options at defensive midfielder reveals how much more tactically mature **Del Moral** is in recognizing the moment when to step forward, and when to stay in cover.

With this tandem, Hajduk finally got what was chronically lacking not only to coach **Garcia**, but also to his predecessors – physical aggression and defensive stability in the heart of the pitch, which significantly facilitates putting the team together for HNL challenges.

sections.subtitle: Enigma in the back line: Is Hajduk's 'wild card' center-back too big a risk for Europe?
sections.screenshot_description: Duje Granić analyzes the play, advantages and flaws of Hajduk's center-backs.
sections.content:
Despite the victory, certain defensive players of Hajduk once again showed worrying oscillations. **Renato Špehar** opened the topic of the left center-back who inexplicably left **Beljo** at the first goal, and later made an unreasonable, dangerous tackle on **Kačavenda** that could easily have ended with a red card. It is a pattern of behavior that repeats itself, given that the same player made similar cardinal mistakes at Rujevica and in appearances for the Kosovo national team.

**Duje Granić** described that defender as a true *wild card* player – he is physically extremely powerful, aggressive, possesses good dribbling and progressive passing, but on the pitch he is completely unrestrained. Although in some matches, like the one against **Raków**, he was among the best on the pitch, his flaws regularly come to light in derbies. Nevertheless, **Granić** believes that in the context of the domestic championship it pays off for Hajduk to live with his mistakes because with his physical predispositions and speed he can compensate for the shortcomings of teammates like **Barišić**, for whom pure defense of the penalty area is not a strong suit.

On the other hand, **Luka Vujić** took a significantly sharper stance, especially in the context of upcoming European tests such as the match with **Ajax**:

- **Vujić** believes that the defender makes too many mistakes in the basic reading of the game and that in the last year he has not progressed in that field at all.
- His excellent performance against **Raków** is the result of the fact that the Polish team cultivates direct, 'dum-dum' football with long balls, where his speed and physical strength come to the fore.
- In the domestic championship, where Hajduk stands high in the opponent's half, he is the only center-back in the squad who can defend depth in a wide space, because of which he will probably keep his place in the starting eleven.
- However, in European matches in which Hajduk will defend in a lower block, such a profile becomes too big a risk and **Vujić** expects his move to the bench, while he rated the center-back acquisition who arrived this summer as the weakest reinforcement of the transfer window.

sections.subtitle: Dinamo's personnel wanderings: A limited right side and failed investments in the transfer window
sections.screenshot_description: Marino Durdov comments on Dinamo's problems on the right side of defense and the limitations of the wing players.
sections.content:
The analysis of Dinamo's defeat began with the surprising personnel solutions on the right side, where a rotational full-back and **Lisica** operated, while both of Hajduk's goals fell precisely through that side. **Marino Durdov** agreed with the statement of Dinamo's coach after the match that the mentioned right-back was no worse than the rest of the team, but ironically noticed that this only means that everyone else was extremely bad.

**Durdov** points out that this is a player who was brought in exclusively for rotation in the cup or after European exhaustions – a typical player for a 'rating of 6.0 to 6.5' who will not make a cardinal mistake, but terribly limits the team in the attacking phase. When **Lisica** – a winger who depends exclusively on open space and depth, which did not exist against Hajduk – is placed in front of such a full-back, who lacks modern offensive characteristics, Dinamo independently cut off its entire right side of the attack. With a completely healthy **Galešić**, who has shown the most this season and had already been tried at full-back, **Durdov** considers such a selection of the starting lineup for the derby senseless.

**Luka Vujić** followed up with a criticism of Dinamo's sports policy and the summer transfer window:

- In previous years, Dinamo brought in the best full-backs from smaller HNL clubs as backup options, whereas now money was saved on players who are at best average first-league players.
- In defense, big problems were also shown by **Dominguez**, whose insecurity and the space between him and the full-back Hajduk purposefully attacked by entering the left half-space.
- The wing positions, which for years were Dinamo's strongest weapon, are now full of question marks. **Oršić** is in a noticeable decline and far from his former level, **Lisica** cannot make a difference continuously, while the newly arrived foreigners have not yet shown any serious impact.
- Despite the invested money, Dinamo is once again reduced to last season's problem from Europe – apart from **Beljo**, in the final third of the pitch there is simply no player the team can rely on to solve the match with individual quality.

sections.subtitle: Why Dinamo remained on one chance: Irreplaceable absences of Mišić and Stojković
sections.screenshot_description: Duje Granić explains how much Dinamo's game misses Josip Mišić and Luka Stojković.
sections.content:
The fact that until the very stoppage time and a chaotic attack Dinamo created only one big chance – the one from which **Beljo** scored a goal – best illustrates the sterility of the Zagreb team at Poljud. **Duje Granić** sees the main cause of such a drop compared to the spring part of last season in the complete collapse of balance in the midfield due to the absences of **Mišić** and **Stojković**.

Last season's midfield was perfectly balanced: **Mišić** acted at the bottom of the midfield as a top creator, while **Stojković** brought enormous energy and played more like a 'ten' than a classic 'eight'. In the Split derby, that balance disappeared:

- It is impossible to replace **Mišić** because no other defensive midfielder in the league has such a range of passing and ability to create from deep.
- **Stojković** was replaced by **Kačavenda**, a player every coach loves because of his energy and versatility (*box-to-box* characteristics), but who is significantly more limited in purely attacking creation.
- An additional problem is the drop in form of **Zajc**, who is playing noticeably weaker this season than last year, and the loss of **Bakar** on the wing, whose goals and contribution were underestimated.

**Marino Durdov** concluded the analysis of Dinamo's offense by emphasizing that the absence of **Mišić** is felt the most in the inability to quickly switch the point of attack from one side to the other. Without those fast diagonals, the limited wingers remain cut off and cannot get into a situation to attack an unsettled defense. As the only real solution for matches in which Dinamo dominates possession, **Durdov** sees the return of **Ivanušec** to true form. Unlike classic, linear wingers like **Hoxha** and **Lisica** who are more useful in European transition matches, in the HNL Dinamo desperately needs noble players who enter the half-space, look for quick combination play, and change the gravity of the attack with their technical abilities.

iterations.theme: Heroes of Hajduk's victory, psychological growth of the team and preview of European tests against Ajax and Anderlecht

sections.subtitle: From a disputed player to the hero of the derby: How Bamba used continuity and open space
sections.screenshot_description: Luka Vujić explains how Bamba attacks open space and why he is key for big matches.
sections.content:
Analyzing the individuals who decided the biggest Croatian derby, host Renato Špehar highlighted Bamba in the foreground, who was named player of the match. His performance against Dinamo was impressive: **one goal scored, six out of seven successful dribbles, two big chances created, and seven out of nine accurate passes**. In doing so, Špehar reminded how Duje Granić, after the European match with Žilina, stated that he would no longer like to see Bamba in Hajduk's jersey, opening the question of whether this wing forward is actually a much better player when he has a well-organized midfield behind him that enables him to play one-on-one.

Luka Vujić believes that Bamba is completely the same player as he was upon his arrival in Split, but that everything comes down to the way he is used and the much-needed continuity. Earlier there was a myth about the so-called "summer Bamba" because at the beginning of the season he would get opportunities in a row, and then he would move to the bench from which he would find it hard to return to rhythm. Now he has played all nine championship rounds, and coach Garcia, who also knew how to get the maximum out of wing players in Istra, found an ideal role for him.

- **Attacking depth:** Bamba is the fastest player of the team who excellently attacks the open space behind the opponent's back line.
- **Trigger for transition:** In big matches, including the upcoming European tests, he is the main target for long balls and pulling counter-attacks.
- **Defensive stability:** In the defensive phase he looks significantly better than before, to which a defensively more stable full-back on the right side contributes, as well as Del Moral who as a right six timely steps out to cover.

Vujić notes that Bamba will never be a 10 or 20 million euro winger nor a player for excessive combination play and dropping deep for the ball, but for **750 thousand euros**, how much Hajduk paid for him, in the right context he justifies the investment multiple times over and has the opportunity to become an "evergreen Bamba" – a player for all seasons.

Duje Granić agreed with that, admitting that no Hajduk player in the last few years has gone from such extremes to extremes. Granić pointed out how Garcia himself emphasized how sensitive Bamba is and how even the slightest falling out of rhythm sets him back. Nevertheless, the biggest merit of the coach is that he believed in him even when fans and analysts did not. In the derby, Bamba, apart from standard speed and energy, also showed above-average decision-making in the final third, such as the timely pass to Šego. Granić concludes that Hajduk on the right side, while Brajković is absent, simply does not have a player profile with such transition and that Bamba, while maintaining focus, can be the club's best winger.

sections.subtitle: Tactical evolution of Šimun Hrgović: Prototype of a modern full-back and a lethal left side
sections.screenshot_description: Tactical display on the screen while Duje Granić analyzes Hrgović's role in breaking Dinamo's pressing.
sections.content:
The second key individual in the analysis was **Šimun Hrgović**, whose role Duje Granić illustrated through graphic displays on the screen. In the attacking build-up phase, Hajduk formed a **3-2-5** (that is, 3-2-4-1) structure, whereby they successfully broke the first line of Dinamo's pressure, which stood in a 4-4-1-1 formation. Granić especially praised Hrgović's tactical intelligence and versatility, which coach Garcia himself also highlighted at the press conference.

Hrgović excellently tucked into the midfield from the left side, achieving fantastic cooperation with his teammate on the left wing. The two of them constantly complemented each other – when Hrgović entered the half-space, the wing player would hold the width, and vice versa. Because of that dynamics, energy, and technical quality, Granić considers the left side the most dangerous part of Hajduk's team, adding that it is no coincidence that both are mentioned in the context of the Croatian national team.

Luka Vujić followed up on the analysis of the build-up play, directing one criticism at Hajduk's expense as well. He believes that the Split team in the derby tested Dinamo's midfield players through the middle too little and found its two "tens" too little, which, paradoxically, it did much better in the first half of the match against Rijeka. Instead, Hajduk too often hoofed long balls to Šego, who did not win a single aerial duel.

Nevertheless, speaking about Hrgović himself, Vujić emphasized the importance of the fact that Garcia uses him as a **prototype of a modern, inverted full-back**:

- **Play in a 3-2-4-1 structure:** In modern football, classic full-backs hardly survive at the top level, and Hrgović managed excellently in the role of a player who enters the middle.
- **Role of one of the two sixes:** Vujić was most impressed by how Hrgović reads the game and finds solutions when he positions himself in a line with the defensive midfielder.
- **Room for improvement:** He manages the weakest when he plays high as one of the two tens because he lacks runs from the second plan and a better quality shot, while in the derby he was extremely useful pulling out wide and sending crosses on the run.

The conclusion is that Hrgović, of all the players who were in the club last season as well, achieved by far the biggest individual progress.

sections.subtitle: Psychological turnaround under Garcia and the circus in stoppage time
sections.screenshot_description: Luka Vujić talks about the psychological growth of Hajduk and belief in victory in difficult conditions.
sections.content:
Summarizing the events on the pitch, Renato Špehar concluded that Hajduk in the derby kept its recognizable style along with a strong defensive stance and finally the right player profiles, while Dinamo lacked stance, quality, and automatisms in play. The last half hour of the match, which turned into "water polo" due to the huge downpour, was impossible to analyze tactically. In those moments of pure survival and test of character, Dinamo could have reached a point via Beljo's post, but the general impression is that Hajduk deservedly celebrated.

In doing so, Luka Vujić highlighted a key, and often neglected factor – **the psychological growth of the team**. He emphasized that he does not remember when Hajduk won at Poljud in a match played in such a flood, since in the past they regularly lost such matches. Under the leadership of Garcia, who recorded his first victory against Dinamo and previously broke the barrier in European qualifiers, the team shows significantly greater belief in itself. That psychological momentum is additionally strengthened by the fact that the coach can now bring in defensively responsible players like Del Moral from the bench.

In the final part of the review of the derby, Špehar opened the topic of the refereeing of **Igor Pajač**, mentioning several disputed situations: a sharp tackle by Kačavenda that went without a yellow card, a potential red card for Raci, and the chaos in stoppage time with a temporary interruption of the match in the 95th minute.

Marino Durdov rated Pajač's refereeing with a passing grade, calling his style "compensation upon compensation", which is standard for referees with longer tenure in the league. Durdov believes that Kačavenda had to get at least a yellow card, while for a final judgment on a potential red card for Raci he lacked a better camera angle from behind. Nevertheless, he emphasized that the referee was not in the foreground, which is always positive. As for the interruption in the 94th minute, Durdov called it complete nonsense, pointing out that a match in that phase must be brought to an end even if "bombs were falling", recalling in doing so a bizarre example from the NBA league about twenty years ago when due to an error by the scorer's table, only the last three minutes of a match were played subsequently, months later.

sections.subtitle: Spectacle in the Conference League: Can Hajduk match the powerful Ajax with its style?
sections.screenshot_description: Duje Granić explains why Hajduk must not give up on its style of play against Ajax.
sections.content:
The victory in the derby was just an overture to a hellish rhythm of five matches in fifteen days, and Hajduk already on Thursday at a sold-out Poljud opens the group stage of the Conference League against **Ajax**. Host Renato Špehar, who recently watched the Dutch giant live in a championship match against Excelsior, shared his observations firsthand. Despite big-name reinforcements, the team is not yet at its peak, and their play largely depends on the phenomenal Oscar on the left side. Špehar believes that the injury of Kasper Dolberg is actually bad news for Hajduk, because he will be replaced by a physically extremely robust and powerful forward who will represent a huge challenge for Šarlija. As Ajax's biggest vulnerability, he highlighted defensive transition and a defense set at 40 meters from the goal, which even the modest Excelsior managed to punish with two goals from counter-attacks.

Duje Granić in the preview of the match points out that he expects a brave approach from Hajduk, without extreme tactical adjustments such as switching to a 5-4-1 formation:

- **Belief in one's own mechanisms:** Hajduk does not have the profile of players for a low block; this team was selected for proactive football and must play the way it plays the entire season.
- **Power of the Poljud stands:** Granić recalled the first 30 minutes of the match against Villarreal, when high pressure along with thunderous support from the stands on every corner or won ball created huge problems for the favored opponent.
- **Breaking European traumas:** After the turnarounds against Rakow and Dinamo, it is visible that the team no longer sinks after conceding a goal, so even a potential heavy defeat by Ajax should not ruin the positive image if the approach is right.

Luka Vujić agreed that Hajduk has nothing to lose in this match, given that it sold out the tickets in just 50 minutes, and waited a full 15 years for a European autumn. He added that Ajax, which was taken over this summer by the former Girona coach **Míchel**, is convincingly the strongest opponent Garcia has met so far. As an opportunity for Hajduk, Vujić sees the space behind the back of Wijndal, the weakest link in Ajax's defense, which Bamba should try to exploit with his runs. On the other hand, he warned that the midfield with Pajaziti, Del Moral, and Pukštas will have to play flawlessly in order to stop the opponent's creation and the extremely wide attacking squad which also includes the expensively paid Marcos Leonardo.

sections.subtitle: Dinamo's period of truth: Analysis of Anderlecht and challenges ahead of Mario Kovačević
sections.screenshot_description: Marino Durdov analyzes Anderlecht's play and previews the upcoming tests for Dinamo.
sections.content:
While European euphoria shakes the Split team, an extremely demanding "period of truth" lies ahead of Dinamo and coach **Mario Kovačević**, which begins with an away match at **Anderlecht**, and continues with matches against Slaven Belupo, Nantes, and Rijeka. Analyzing the Belgian representative, Marino Durdov stylistically compared it to Genk, whom Dinamo met last season, assessing that Anderlecht is perhaps only half a notch weaker as a team.

Durdov highlighted several key characteristics of Dinamo's next opponent:

- **Speed and verticality:** From the first to the ninetieth minute, Anderlecht insists on fast combination play with the goal of entering deep into the opponent's penalty area.
- **Lethality from close range:** According to statistical data, the Belgian team scored all of this season's goals in the championship inside 16 meters, looking exclusively for shots with a high conversion rate.
- **Excellent form:** In the domestic championship they are undefeated since the end of August, and their only recent defeat was inflicted on them by Lyon in the first round of the Europa League.

Given the insecurities shown in the derby by Dominguez and McKenna, Durdov expects that Kovačević will include **Galešić** in the starting eleven, either at the center-back position or at right-back. While maximum concentration will be necessary in the defensive phase, offensively Dinamo will depend on the individual genius of Stojković, the proven output of Beljo, and the final awakening of the wing players.

Looking at the bigger picture of the upcoming schedule, Durdov believes that Slaven Belupo in the domestic championship should not represent too big an obstacle even for such a shaken Dinamo, but will serve as a transitional match. However, he expressed great skepticism ahead of the clash with the French **Nantes**, emphasizing that the current Dinamo team seems completely unprepared for such a style of play and level of intensity, while they will be able to say more about the later derby with Rijeka only when they see how the team will react to the first two tests.
